plain_language: Hoy, otros dos servidores AI abiertos lanzaron carga de modelo a prueba de manipulación por defecto. El recuento de errores de herramientas de agente alcanzó nueve en una semana. Doce países comparten una lista de verificación AI.
findings:
(Del resumen en inglés de hoy) Wednesday's cycle consolidates Tuesday's signed-checkpoint and runtime-verifier landings into a three-tier mitigation default-shipment cadence and extends the agentic-AI tooling-stack CVE wave to its first workflow-state-path-tier instance while widening the Indo-Pacific cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter to twelve named jurisdictions with the first formal Latin American mirror-signature commitment plus the first African exploratory observer. On the agentic-AI security axis, AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 (CVSS 8.6, May 13) drops Wednesday-morning Pacific as a path-traversal vulnerability in the workflow-state checkpoint loader, mirroring the LangGraph CVE-2026-44712 deserialization pattern but with a different exploitation surface; AutoGen ships v0.6.4 same-day plus a backport advisory for v0.5.x and v0.4.x referenced by the NHS England blocklist, and the Trail of Bits Tuesday taxonomy extends from eight to nine agent-checkpoint-and-manifest-loader CVEs (adding AutoGen workflow-state path-traversal to the eight prior taxonomy entries spanning CrewAI, Haystack, AutoGen prior manifest-fetcher entry, Semantic Kernel, LangChain, LangGraph, LiteLLM, and Pydantic AI). DeepMind plus Meta AI plus Anthropic plus Microsoft co-publish a Wednesday joint follow-up addendum v2 (Runtime Signature-Verification and Manifest-Allowlist Enforcement v2, arxiv 2605.06712v2) extending the Tuesday runtime-verifier paper with a workflow-state path-canonicalization integration pattern; Microsoft, LangChain, CrewAI, the Pydantic AI maintainer team, and the AutoGen maintainer team commit Wednesday to ship the three-tier mitigation as default in the next minor-version release alongside the load-time signed-checkpoint primitive and the runtime manifest-allowlist-validation primitive, with the coordinated mid-June default-shipment target now spanning all three tier surfaces.

On the substrate-and-serving axis the three-tier reference implementation lands in production form across two stack tiers in the same Wednesday window. SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 ships a Wednesday point release adding the Sigstore-or-cosign-compatible signature-verified checkpoint loader AND defaults it as the documented default load path for new installs (with an explicit unsigned-load opt-out flag for sandboxed test fixtures), making SGLang the second open-source serving stack to ship the primitive AND the first to default it; Hugging Face TGI v3.2.0 ships a parallel Wednesday point release adding the signed-checkpoint loader and shipping it as the documented default load path simultaneously with SGLang, making TGI the third open-source serving stack to ship the primitive. Unsloth's Wednesday changelog ships a kernel-fused tensor-parallel router-attention forward-and-backward pass on quad-Hopper workstation tiers reporting a further 11 percent training-step time reduction plus a 7 percent peak combined VRAM reduction on Llama 4 Behemoth router-only training plus a deterministic workflow-state path-canonicalization mitigation tied to the AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 disclosure — Unsloth becomes the first local-LLM fine-tuning stack to ship the workflow-state mitigation alongside the signed-checkpoint primitive ahead of the framework cohort's coordinated mid-June default-shipment target now extended to cover all three tier surfaces — alongside an extended INT8 ONNX export path for the AMD MI350 deployment cohort, a community-contributed Mistral Magistral 22B Mixture-of-Experts recipe at 6 percent peak combined VRAM on a dual-RTX 6000 Ada workstation, and a Hacker News reproduction of the Qwen3.7-32B router-only recipe through the new workflow-state mitigation at 11 percent peak combined VRAM on an Apple Mac Pro 2026 M5 Ultra. Yotta Labs canonical benchmarks place the shared-prefix workload at approximately 17,140 tok/s on vLLM v0.11.3 versus 18,860 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 (throughput gap holds at 9.1 percent flat from Tuesday), and Cloudflare Infire reports the L40S edge-tier Infire advantage closes to 1.12x (vs 1.18x Tuesday) with parity projected at the vLLM v0.11.4 late-May window targeting Monday May 18. Stable Long-Context RL via Router-Aware Advantage Decomposition v6 (arxiv 2605.05844 v6) closes the long-context training-stability gap on the new quad-Hopper kernel-fused setup with pre-tested integration against the vLLM v0.11.3 plus SGLang RadixArk v0.5.7 plus TGI v3.2.0 signed-checkpoint loaders simultaneously — the first three-stack training-and-serving end-to-end formal-verification chain at the local-LLM workstation tier — and Verifiable Workflow-State Path Canonicalization for Agentic AI Multi-Tier Loaders (arxiv 2605.06799) supplies the formal-verification anchor with reference implementations in Python and Rust covering all nine CVE-pattern instances.

On the policy-and-procurement axis the May 15 14:00 EDT S-407 classified threshold briefing enters its two-business-day window with a firmed seven-witness slate (Department of Energy Cyber Security, Energy Security, and Emergency Response Assistant Secretary joins as seventh witness alongside NIST Director Locascio, ODNI cyber lead, NSA Cybersecurity Directorate director, Microsoft MSTIC representative, CISA Director, and FCC PSHSB Bureau Chief), the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology issues a Wednesday-afternoon follow-up press release confirming a coordinated bicameral request bundle with the Senate Cyber Subcommittee for the parallel 30-day House technical review window, and the American Bar Association Cybersecurity Legal Task Force plus the National Association of Attorneys General AI working group file a Wednesday amicus letter joining the fourteen-organization coalition narrowing focus to the per-state attorney-general consultation pathway plus the AISI cyber-evaluation reciprocity 120-day placement window alignment; OSTP holds its line that the draft remains in interagency review with no signing window before May 22. The Indo-Pacific reciprocity perimeter reaches its first twelve-jurisdiction count (Brazil's ANCiber publishes a Wednesday entry note converting prior interest into a formal exploratory-observer commitment with a 240-day national-consultation window targeting Q2 2027 mirror signature) plus the first African entry (South Africa's Cybersecurity Hub plus the Department of Communications and Digital Technologies announce a parallel exploratory-observer track with a 270-day consultation window — the first cross-continental extension since the Latin American Tuesday landing), with the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat publishing a Wednesday procedural note describing the cohort as on track toward thirteen-jurisdiction formal mirror count by Q3 2026. OpenAI's ChatGPT Enterprise per-org agent registry GA extends Wednesday to South-Korea-cloud and Australia-cloud tenants across Microsoft Azure plus AWS Bedrock plus Google Cloud Vertex simultaneously, doubling the Indo-Pacific sovereign-cloud GA-tier coverage from two regions to four (168 enterprise customers by Wednesday business close, up from 87 Tuesday) — with Codex CLI v3.1.1 shipping the workflow-state path-canonicalization mitigation; Mistral Workflows day-thirteen adds Spain's Agencia Estatal de Administracion Tributaria as the fifth central-government sovereign-cloud reference (paid tenancy crosses 348 enterprise customers, daily-execution count past 5.9M) and the four-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix moves from private preview to public preview.

On the production-exposure side Shadowserver day-thirteen n8n CVE-2026-21858 scan continues the descent to approximately 3,580 internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances (-15.0 percent from Tuesday) with US at 1,160 and India at 605 and the long-tail unpatched share at 25 percent; Censys honeypot exploitation attempts moderate from Tuesday's 4.7x baseline to 3.2x baseline at Wednesday 09:00 UTC; Microsoft Defender for Cloud, CrowdStrike Falcon, and SentinelOne Singularity publish a Wednesday joint follow-on telemetry note adding Manjusaka and Empire to the C2-framework attribution alongside Tuesday's five frameworks, providing the first cross-vendor seven-framework C2 attribution baseline; CISA refreshes the KEV catalog with a Wednesday reminder that the May 21 federal-civilian remediation deadline now sits at T-minus-8 business days, with the CISA federal-civilian operational-directive working draft incorporating the Trail of Bits eight-CVE taxonomy reaching the formal interagency-review window per Wednesday wire reporting. Sysdig's Wednesday morning note reports the median time-from-MCP-server-provisioning to first credential-extraction-attempt on unprotected estates holds at 5 minutes (the second consecutive day at that floor) while Defender-protected tenants extend to approximately 4.4 hours — the gap holds the 50x baseline established Tuesday with the protected-tenant detection latency improving in parallel; Wiz Research reports Microsoft Defender for Cloud's MCP-server quarantine rate hits 39 percent of net-new MCP servers (vs 36 percent Tuesday), the third consecutive day of quarantine-rate expansion; Cisco-Astrix MCP-server identity-gateway tenancy crosses 1,720 enterprise tenants (+17 percent vs Tuesday) with Akamai SkyAtlas MCP-firewall at 920 tenants; and CrowdStrike Falcon for Agentic AI extends the Tuesday public preview rolling out a Wednesday Vertex AI Agent Governance Center managed-interop visibility integration, lifting cross-vendor agentic-AI control-plane visibility to 81 percent of new MCP-server provisioning events — the first time cross-vendor coverage crosses the 80 percent threshold.

On the capital-markets axis Cerebras CBRS prints a textbook second-trading-week consolidation: opening at $195.40 (+0.7 percent from Tuesday's $194.10 close), intraday range tight at $193.80-$197.60, closing at $195.80, trailing-five-session turnover crossing $5.6B, institutional-buyside cumulative net position estimated at 33 percent of float, and a 3.6x call-skew at 14:00 EDT (the second-widest since the IPO debut session); Bernstein holds its $172 Market-Perform floor pending Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close visibility but acknowledges the consolidation materially reduces the single-counterparty concentration discount, while Morgan Stanley reiterates the $192 best-ideas-list target plus adds an explicit upside-tilt scenario at $235 conditional on Saudi MoU closure and Wells Fargo Securities initiates Buy at $208. The SEC Division of Corporation Finance posts a Wednesday EDGAR release pairing a second sample comment letter on AI-services-revenue measurement basis with a topical comment template on hyperscaler-anchor warrant-equity counterparty disclosure shape; SambaNova publishes a Wednesday confidential-submission cover-letter draft for late-June filing referencing the Tenstorrent confidential acknowledgement as the operative precedent; Groq's process pulls forward into the 21-45 day window with the Saudi Aramco Digital MoU close described as on track for late-Q2 2026. Cerebras's Wednesday investor-relations call materials confirm post-IPO manufacturing-capacity expansion pulls OpenAI's first-batch engineering-sample shipment forward from late-Q1 2027 to mid-Q1 2027; Nvidia Vera Rubin second-batch NVL576 engineering samples ship to OpenAI plus Meta plus CoreWeave ahead of Q4 2026 cadence; AMD MI450 first Helios production-rack samples extend to Alibaba Cloud plus Baidu PaddlePaddle Cloud joining Tencent Cloud; Tenstorrent's fifth-wave shipment cadence lifts cumulative racks to 110 against the 280-rack first-half target with the first Spanish sovereign-cloud entry (Telefonica Tech) under the OVHcloud-anchored Gaia-X framework, and the AMD Helios commitment book crosses 9.2GW. The Mag-7 print-cycle preview cohort (Bernstein, Wells Fargo Securities, Evercore ISI, Citi Research, Jefferies) lifts the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability to 78 percent (from 72 percent Tuesday) at the May 21 analyst day, with AWS now expected to ship a fiscal-Q3 2026 AI Services breakout alongside Meta in the same quarter.

On the physical-AI side the Tesla Optimus Gen 3 fourth cohort of 12 units activates at the Fremont cell-pickup-plus-torque-fastening task station bringing the active count to 48 of the 240-unit allocation with cycle-time tightening to 1.08x human-baseline (vs Tuesday's 1.10x), and Tesla Robotics posts a Wednesday 240-second clip of eighteen units performing a coordinated four-station hand-off chain across all three shifts — day-shift, swing-shift, and overnight-shift cohorts — the first three-shift coordination demonstration in production. Stellantis confirms the Detroit 60-unit pilot still activates June 8; Volkswagen Wolfsburg signals interest in a parallel 60-unit Optimus pilot for fiscal H2 2026 (a fresh OEM commitment beyond Tuesday's Atlas-only Wolfsburg pilot). BMW Group's Spartanburg production-line operations team confirms a Wednesday 30-unit Atlas allocation on the assembly-line under-body conveyor task, joining the BMW Group humanoid roster that already includes the Figure 03 Spartanburg 14-day production run cohort — the first time a single OEM operates two humanoid platforms in production at the same site, a structural inflection in the four-OEM-adopted humanoid league-table thesis. Volkswagen Wolfsburg pilot scales from 24-unit to 40 units (a Wednesday 16-unit expansion). Hyundai Robotics Metaplant Dangjin rolling-mill pickup motion cycle-time improvement stabilizes at 4.8 percent (up from 4.6 percent Tuesday). On the platform-attestation side, Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 day-six registry telemetry shows a Wednesday continuation of the second-week growth-rate normalization — 23,210 published skills (up from 21,640 Tuesday, +7.3 percent, the third sub-15-percent daily gain and first sub-10-percent reading), 2.32M skill installs across the sixth 24 hours, 48 auto-quarantined Mythos-class skills (up from 42 Tuesday) — with Spain's Indra Sistemas, Sweden's Saab Kockums, Singapore's ST Engineering, and Israel's Rafael Advanced Defense Systems signing the contractual ethics-and-misuse rider on Wednesday business open lifting the gated cohort to 56 enterprise customers and extending the rider's reach to the Mediterranean-plus-Indo-Pacific allied defense industrial base; Simon Willison's Wednesday extended note documents that the open-source verification harness now produces a deterministic per-tenant attestation-log audit trail across all 56 gated tenants with cross-tenant compositional safety checks completing in under 75 seconds via Stanford CIS batch-processing optimization.

Dormant-pool reactivations land cleanly on the day's evidence: the Physical AI league tables rank top-five OEM-adopted humanoids prediction (Apr 25) revives on the Tesla Fremont 48-unit Gen 3 cohort plus the BMW Spartanburg Atlas allocation plus the Volkswagen Wolfsburg Optimus signaling plus the Hyundai Metaplant Dangjin stabilization; the Agent registry standard converges with MCP for agent artifacts prediction (Apr 19) revives on the OpenAI per-org agent registry second-wave Indo-Pacific GA plus the four-vendor cross-orchestrator interop matrix public preview transition plus Codex CLI v3.1.1 workflow-state path-canonicalization mitigation; the Indirect prompt injection becomes a top CVE category prediction (Apr 19) revives on AutoGen CVE-2026-44918 at the workflow-state path tier plus the nine-CVE Trail of Bits taxonomy plus the CISA federal-civilian operational-directive working-draft interagency-review entry. Cross-stream coherence is high across security, policy, capital markets, and physical AI, with the day's coordinated three-tier mitigation plus signed-checkpoint default-shipment landing the structural inflection at the workstation-and-serving tiers.
